examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Alternate Forms of the Cotangent-Cosecant Identity
examples.worked_solution:
Note that we can simplify this expression by transforming the denominator into a form where we can apply a known trigonometric identity.

First, we multiply the numerator and the denominator of our expression by $\csc \theta + \cot \theta.$ This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta -\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the identity $\csc^2 \theta - \cot^2 \theta=1$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta -{cot}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta }{1} \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta +\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Using the identity $1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta ={csc}^{2}⁡\theta ,$ we rewrite and simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+{cot}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } & =\frac{{csc}^{2}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{cot}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$
